audit.priority_existing_gap: US housing 2006 matched price/rent index would fill an applicable valuation gap; US1873 matched railroad revenue/net income and capital investment population would best serve infrastructure analogy. Neither matched ratio acquired in this bounded pass.
audit.acquired_ancillary_case: UK railway mania 1845; not one of current ten reader historicalCases
existing_limitations: Japan NRI350 earnings population differs from Nikkei225 price index
China year-end Shanghai P/E is not peak-month P/E
US broad-market CAPE is context, not Nasdaq or AI-sector P/E
Dotcom MSFT/INTC survivors are not failed startups or telecom population

series.population: British railway industry as compiled in source Table 1
series.source_table: Table 1, printed page 8; PDF page index 7
series.underlying_provenance: Footnote 8, printed page 54: derived from Tooke and Newmarch, A History of Prices, vol. 5 (1857), p.352. Author notes alternative sources differ. Underlying original not separately acquired.
series.ratio_definition: Annual revenue per mile divided by construction cost per mile, same row/population; gross annual revenue relative to accumulated construction cost.
caveats: Gross revenue is before operating expenses, interest and taxes
Construction cost is not annual capex or market capitalization
Old and new lines are aggregated; not an incremental new-line return
Source accounting/provenance differs from modern cash-flow statements
Rounded source inputs; display derived ratio to one decimal at most
Do not splice into US1873 or modern capex/OCF series
